Injini is Putting $125,000 Behind AI Built for African Classrooms
text_paragraph_1: Africa’s leading EdTech accelerator Injini, is committing $125,000 to a new venture-building initiative that will take early-stage teams across Southern Africa from ideation to market-ready EdTech startups.
text_paragraph_2: The eight-month AI Venture Builder and Incubation Programme, supported by Coefficient Giving, opened applications on September 7 and will select 12 pre-formed teams from nine countries. Applicants must be based in Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho, Malawi, Mozambique, Namibia, South Africa, Zambia or Zimbabwe.
text_paragraph_3: Unlike a conventional accelerator that backs startups with existing products or traction, Injini is targeting teams still at the ideation stage. Their concepts, however, must address one of the program’s five focus areas : foundational learning; teacher capacity and classroom support; learner pathways and futures; inclusion and access; or ecosystem and engagement.

text_paragraph_1: The Export-Import Bank of Korea will establish a strategic project identification system centered on the six major national strategic industries of Uzbekistan.
text_paragraph_2: The Export-Import Bank of Korea announced on Sep. 15 that it signed a ‘Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) for the Establishment of a Strategic Project Identification System’ with the Ministry of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistan. This agreement was carried out in the presence of President Lee Jae-myung and Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev during the Korea-Uzbekistan Summit, which was held on the occasion of the first Korea-Central Asia Summit. Export-Import Bank of Korea President Hwang Ki-yeon and Minister of Investment, Industry and Trade of Uzbekistan Laziz Kudratov stepped forward as the signatories.
text_paragraph_3: The areas of cooperation encompass the entirety of the six major national strategic industries promoted by Uzbekistan. Specifically, they include 1) critical minerals, 2) artificial intelligence (AI) and digital, 3) advanced infrastructure, 4) the creation of specialized industrial complexes exclusively for Korean companies, and 5) pharmaceuticals and biotechnology. The Export-Import Bank of Korea plans to preemptively identify promising projects that are mutually beneficial to both countries and specify the financial support measures necessary for project implementation.
